verified_facts: FM's person property getter returned the tofP foot record for all 17 managed first-team players with no player screen open, on FM's UI thread, with manager, date, club, and squad unchanged.
Two runs produced identical categories, and FM's label mapper returned Left Only, Left, Right Only, Right, and Either for categories 0 to 4.

Four runs in total, including one after FM was restarted into a different process with a different UI thread, produced identical footedness for all 17 players, so the result does not depend on one process or one set of addresses.
Every run left FM alive with its process identity, module base, manager, date, club, and squad hash unchanged, and released the Windows Frida server.
limitations: The two prototype reports do not embed manager or date identity; the controller session reports do.
Values have not yet been compared with FM's player screens, so footedness is cold-query-proven but not ui-verified.
Scope is the managed first team only; external players need the scouted-person path.

verified_facts: Calling FM's proven visible-attribute builder in-process, via Frida, for all 17 managed players and all 41 display attributes in one session produced 697 observations, all visibility=known, with no player screen open.
Every one of those 697 values matched tools/fm20_owned_visible_source.py's independent raw-byte production reader exactly, with zero mismatches.

verified_facts: Replaying FM's full player-search filter against the observed Player Search context returned true for a transfer-listed external player, false for a non-transfer-listed external player, and false for an own first-team player, matching every expectation.
The filter's active rule set at the time included PERSON_TRANSFER_LISTED_FILTER_RULE, so a false verdict for a non-transfer-listed player is correct behaviour rather than a failed replay.
The cold replay is therefore not missing live state; an earlier conclusion to the contrary rested on a sample with no player expected to pass.
Manager, game date, search arguments, and source IDs were unchanged across the run.
limitations: This proves the filter replays faithfully; it does not establish that the filter is the discoverability boundary. The rule set shows it is the manager's current search criteria.
The search source, not this filter, is the candidate for the discoverable universe, and that identification is still unverified against FM's displayed result count.

verified_facts: FM's player-search filter was evaluated for all 4,953 pool players entirely cold: no Player Search observation, no captured runtime context, and no operator interaction. A synthetic context supplying only the manager interface and team pointers was sufficient once the manager's own search criteria were cleared.
Calling the composite evaluator at 0x42c96a0 directly, rather than the wrapper at 0x5337010, removes the wrapper's thread constraint and allows the batch to run on FM's busy UI thread.
The replay accepted 4,934 players against the 4,933 FM displays for the same package and cleared criteria, a single-player difference.
All 19 rejections were the manager's own club players, which is exactly how many of the club's 20 players are present in the pool.

The pool tracked a scouting-package change made in-game with no change on the reading side: it read 4,340 under no package and 4,953 under the Vanarama North/South package, against 4,320 and 4,933 displayed.
limitations: One player accepted by the replay is not displayed by FM. The cause is unidentified and the difference is in the unsafe direction, so the set is a superset of FM's by one and must not be treated as an exact match.
The product owner accepted this tolerance on 16 September 2026 rather than blocking on it.
Verified for one manager, one save, and two package states only.

Whether primary/Natural positions can themselves ever be gated is untested; both observed here were fully known.

verified_facts: FM's TACTICAL_ROLE_LABEL and DUTY_POPUP_BUTTON consume separate tdPT and lrPT properties. The tactic-slot getter masks a full 64-bit word with 0x406e00000 for duty and 0x7fffbf91fdeff for role.

The tactic-slot serializer writes position as u32 and role/duty as u64. Existing match archives contain structurally valid tactic-array prefixes with these words, independently of the app's configured tactics.
MATCH_MANAGER serializes two tactic arrays per manager, at native +0xa20 and +0x17e0. They must not be treated as a home/away pair.

The stable survey retained 53 unambiguous first-team fixture candidates containing 566 valid tactic prefixes and rejected three ambiguous fixture/chunk candidates. State invariants and all four archive hashes remained unchanged.

For Hungerford versus Braintree on 28 March 2020, the named Vertical 4-4-2 prefix has CM Support at position 0x200400 and CM Defend at 0x100400; another default prefix reverses them. Both players have role-only code 0x20.
limitations: No tactic prefix is bound to a historical appearance. Team, snapshot time, override meaning, substitutions and in-match changes remain unverified.

The named 28 March prefix agrees with the earlier operator confirmation (Bellamy 92314 at 0x200400 Support, Hargreaves 100628 at 0x100400 Defend); a reported conflict was a swap of the two short IDs, corrected 4 October 2026. One match does not establish team ownership.
Prefix boundaries stop after player overrides, before variable set pieces and trailing settings. They are not full-array ends.
Only Defend, Support and Attack are labeled; Stopper, Cover and Automatic remain unlabelled masks. Historical UI comparison is pending.
This is research-only evidence and does not replace application inference or modify captures/history.
The earlier exploratory session ending 201017207456Z predates ambiguous fixture rejection and its counts are superseded.
